Corning has not confirmed the date; calendars show Oct 27 (MarketBeat estimate), Oct 28 08:30 (AJ Bell, which matches the Oct 28, 2025 pattern) and Nov 3 (TipRanks, based on past reporting), and all three fall inside the window. Guidance, rechecked in the Q2 8-K Ex.99: core sales about +16% to $4.9-5.0B and core EPS about +28% to $0.85-0.89. Corning beat the top of its own EPS guide in Q1 and Q2. The supervisor corrected the release-day reactions: the last four were all negative (Oct 28, 2025 -3.3%, Jan 28 -5.0%, Apr 28 -8.9%, Jul 28 -12.1%). Four points are too few to tilt the centre, but together with the $2B ATM overhang (Sep 11 8-K) they argue against a positive skew. I keep a near-symmetric lognormal with sigma about 18% for the month (annual vol / 3.5 plus an earnings bump), centred just below spot (~$156). The 1-month ladder is unchanged from round 1. fair_value.method: Blend of 26x Oct-2027 NTM core EPS $5.10 = $133 (70%; 27x consistent-basis peer level less 3% for net probability-weighted post-horizon risks) and a 2027-2033 FCF DCF at 9.6% WACC / 4% terminal growth with the same risk overlay = $111 (30%): 0.7 x 132.6 + 0.3 x 110.8 = $126. Core EPS already bears stock-based compensation.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM core EPS at Oct-2027 $5.10 (0.25 x FY27 $4.37 + 0.75 x FY28E $5.34; SBC already expensed in core EPS) x 26x (27x peer-based less 3% net post-horizon risk) = $132.6

inputs_detail.derivation: Re-opened 2026-10-12: FY27 $4.37 (S&P Global via StockAnalysis); FY26 $3.29; FY27 revenue $23.10B

The FY27 consensus has EPS +33% on revenue +19.6% ($19.31B->$23.10B, src 11). The Q3 guide is EPS +28% on sales +16% (src 1). Management's 19% sales CAGR Q4'26-Q4'30 with earnings growing faster than sales (src 1/9) implies sales of roughly +17-19% in FY28, and 1.3x leverage on that gives about +22-25%. I take +24%, up from round 1's +22% because the guide leverage is verified, but below the supervisor's +25% because leverage should fade as the capacity ramp adds depreciation (capex rising in H2 per the call, src 9).
$2.0B / $156.68 = 12.8M shares on 875M core diluted shares (src 1) = 1.46%. The NVIDIA 15M @ $180 warrant adds only about 1.5M treasury-method shares at $200 (src 4), so it is ignored.

inputs_detail.input: NTM EPS at horizon (Oct-27 to Sep-28)

inputs_detail.derivation: I rebuilt every peer on one consistent consensus-NTM basis (price at Oct 9 close / calendarised Oct-26 to Sep-27 EPS from the StockAnalysis forecast pages), which fixes the vendor 'forward P/E' basis error the supervisor flagged. Results for 10 peers: TEL 16.8, CLS 20.6, FN 25.5, APH 27.5, CRDO 28.1, VRT 28.3, COHR 29.6, CIEN 39.3, LITE 43.7, ANET 43.8. The median is 28.2x and the range 16.8-43.8x. GLW's FY27 EPS growth of +33% is below the peer median next-year growth of about +42%, and about 47% of its sales are slower or cyclical segments. Peers with similar growth (APH +24% at 27.5x, VRT +36% at 28.3x) sit at about 27.5-28x. That gives 27x before long-dated risks. Then I apply the net probability-weighted effect of risks after the horizon (see long_dated_risks): -$6.6 fibre-price normalisation, -$1.0 LTA renegotiation ~2029, -$1.0 further equity issuance, -$0.5 hollow-core substitution, +$5.0 co-packaged/scale-up optics content = -$4.1/share on 27 x 5.10 = $137.7, i.e. -3.0%: 27 x 0.97 = 26.2x, rounded to 26x. The AI-capex-slowdown risk is shared by every peer and so already sits in the peer multiple; it is carried in the bear scenario instead. The result, 26x, is inside the 16.8-43.8x range and about 8% below the 28.2x median. GLW today trades at 156.68 / (0.25x3.29 + 0.75x4.37 = $4.10) = 38.2x.

inputs_detail.value: Already expensed in core EPS (no add-back); no further deduction
inputs_detail.derivation: In the Q2 2026 8-K Ex.99 GAAP-to-core reconciliation (GAAP $0.64 -> core $0.78), the lines are hedged exposures, translation, translated-earnings contract, acquisition costs, discrete tax, restructuring, pension MTM, investment loss and gain on sale. There is no stock-based compensation add-back. SBC (cash-flow line 'Share-based compensation expense': $135M Q2, $250M H1 2026) is therefore already charged in the $0.78 and in the consensus $4.37 built on it. Deducting it again would double count. Dilution from equity awards is already in the 875M core diluted shares. Peer basis: StockAnalysis peer EPS is labelled 'non-GAAP adjusted', and I have not verified each peer's SBC treatment at source. If peers exclude SBC, their SBC-inclusive multiples would be higher than shown, so applying them to GLW's SBC-burdened EPS is conservative for GLW. I make no upward adjustment because it is unverified.

inputs_detail.derivation: $4.37 consensus EPS x ~885M diluted shares (875M Q2 core diluted + ATM)

Corrected rationale. Q2 8-K Ex.99 (re-opened): H1 2026 adjusted FCF $1,611M includes a +$709M line for customer deposits and government incentives (Q2 +$880M). H1 core NI = $612M (Q1, src 2) + $680M (Q2, src 1) = $1,292M. Ex-deposit H1 FCF = $1,611M - $709M = $902M = 70% of core NI (round 1 said ~47%, which was wrong). With deposits/prepayments under long-term agreements continuing and capex rising in H2 (call, src 9), 75% sits between ex-deposit (70%) and reported (125%) conversion, weighted toward the former.
Management's 19% sales CAGR Q4'26-Q4'30 with earnings growing faster than sales; FCF grows faster early as capex intensity falls from the build-out peak, then fades.
10Y Treasury par yield on 2026-10-09, re-confirmed on treasury.gov on 2026-10-12 (10/09 row: 10 Yr 5.24). Round 1 used an unsourced ~4.2%.
Damodaran implied ERP, Oct 1, 2026
5y beta, StockAnalysis statistics

Ke = 5.24% + 1.12 x 4.20% = 9.94%. Debt weight = $8.4B debt (10-Q) / (~$135B market cap + $8.4B) = ~6%, at an after-tax cost of about 5.24% x (1-0.21) = 4.1% (Treasury floor, no spread assumed). WACC = 0.94 x 9.94% + 0.06 x 4.1% = 9.6%.
Total debt $8,424M - cash $2,504M at Jun 30, 2026 = $5,920M
875M core diluted + 12.8M ATM ($2.0B / $156.68) = ~888M, rounded to 890M
Springboard targets ($40B run rate by 2030) imply growth continuing past 2030; 4% after a 7-year fade, below the 5.24% nominal risk-free rate

The same net long-dated effect as the P/E leg (-$4.1 on $137.7 = -3.0%), applied to the DCF: 114.2 x 0.97 = $110.8. These risks are not in the DCF's normal growth fade (28%->7%), which assumes no fibre price reset.
FCF starts from core net income, which is after SBC (no SBC add-back in the core reconciliation, Q2 8-K Ex.99), so SBC is treated as an expense, not added back to cash flow.

Optical growth slows to low teens, Glass and Auto are flat, Solar losses persist. NTM EPS about $4.4 at about 20x (lower peer half: CLS 20.6x, TEL 16.8x): 4.4 x 20 = $88.

Scale-up/co-packaged optics content becomes visible (management's $10B photonics revenue stream by 2030; CRU sees CPO fibre demand picking up in 2029-30), and FY28 EPS reaches about $5.8. comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: GLW trades at 38.2x consensus NTM today (156.68 / $4.10). We apply 26x NTM at the horizon: 27x from peer positioning (growth below the peer median) less 3% for net post-horizon risks. That is inside the range and about 8% below the 28.2x median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium. The small discount rests on three points. (1) GLW's FY27 EPS growth of +33% is below the peer median of about +42%, and the peers nearest in growth (APH +24% at 27.5x, VRT +36% at 28.3x) trade at about 27.5-28x. (2) About 47% of Q2 core sales ($2,228M of $4,738M: Glass Innovations, Automotive, Life Sciences) come from slower segments; with cyclical Solar the non-optical share is 56% ($2,666M) [citation gate 2026-10-12: segment list corrected, figures per src 1]. (3) Growth is funded by equity (the $2B ATM and NVIDIA warrants) and customer deposits rather than internal cash. Mitigant: contracted multi-year agreements ($2.7B contract liabilities, 10-Q). The discount is kept small because these factors are partly priced in the growth difference already. Post-horizon: GLW-specific risks not shared by the AI-optics peers (fibre price normalisation as Prysmian/Fujikura capacity arrives, LTA resets around 2029) net of scale-up optics upside cost about 3% more (see long_dated_risks). Basis note: GLW core EPS includes SBC as a cost, while peer consensus is 'non-GAAP adjusted' and may exclude SBC. That mismatch would make peers look cheaper than on GLW's basis, so the discount is conservative and not adjusted further (peer SBC treatment unverified).

thesis_break_reason: Roughly 24x the verified FY27 consensus of $4.37 (4.37 x 24.3 = $106), about 7% below the Jul 28, 2026 post-earnings intraday low of $114.50. It is ~16% below my $126 fair value.

long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Optical Comms is ~44% of Q2 core sales ($2,072M of $4,740M). Assume a ~5% price give-back on ~$12B of 2029 optical sales: ~$0.6B EBIT, ~$0.48B after 20% tax, ~$0.54/share, ~10% of EPS from 2029 onward. Management says price 'is higher' but is not the main profit driver (Q2 call), which caps the size.

Optical growth flat for ~2 years and Springboard misses even the high-confidence plan ($27B by end-2028, $35B by end-2030). 2029 EPS ~20% below base. If priced at the horizon, value falls to ~$100 (-$35). The 10-K lists 'fluctuations in telecommunication and hyperscale data center capital spending' as an Optical risk.

reverse_dcf_check: The horizon price of 26x x $5.10 = $132.6 implies an Oct-2027 EV of $132.6 x 890M + $5.9B net debt = $123.9B. Starting from NTM FCF of $3.40B ($5.10 x 890M x 75%), at a 9.6% WACC and 3.5% terminal growth, that EV requires about 15.5% FCF CAGR for 10 years (2028-2037). One profile that gets close ($124/share): (a) sales +15% a year to 2030, in line with management's high-confidence plan ($35B run rate by end-2030 from ~$20B exiting 2026), then +9% a year to 2037; (b) net margin rising from 17.6% (FY28E: $4.75B NI on ~$27.0B sales = 23.10 x 1.17) to 19% (FY27 consensus is already 16.8% = 3.87/23.10; core operating margin 20.9% in Q2 with management guiding 'at or above 20%'); (c) FCF conversion rising from 75% to ~90% as capex intensity falls after the build. Plausibility: this is a base case in which AI optical demand persists. It is demanding given the long-dated risks above: a 60% chance of a fibre price reset as Prysmian/Fujikura capacity lands, contract resets around 2029, and a 30% chance of capex digestion. That is why I take 26x rather than the 28.2x peer median and keep the explicit-fade DCF (which already implies a slower path, $111) at 30% weight. Before the cut, 27x would need about 16% FCF CAGR. SBC is already a cost in the EPS and FCF used here.
reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor found three errors in my round-1 work, and I verified the fixes at source. (1) The peer 'forward P/E' I took from StockAnalysis statistics pages is on a lagged EPS basis. I re-opened all 10 retained peers' forecast pages and rebuilt price / calendarised NTM consensus EPS myself. My results (APH 27.5, VRT 28.3, CIEN 39.3, LITE 43.7, COHR 29.6, TEL 16.8, ANET 43.8, FN 25.5, CRDO 28.1, CLS 20.6) match the supervisor's figures; the median is 28.2x on my 10 (the supervisor's 27.5x includes PRY and other names I did not use). BDC was dropped. (2) My trailing EV/EBITDA was mislabelled as forward; it is now null. (3) The ex-deposit FCF conversion is about 70%, not 47%: the Q2 8-K Ex.99 shows +$709M of H1 customer deposits/incentives against $1,611M adjusted FCF and $1,292M H1 core NI. My 75% FY27 assumption stands, with the corrected rationale. New evidence of my own: the 10Y Treasury was 5.24% on Oct 9 (round 1 used an unsourced 4.2%) and Damodaran's implied ERP was 4.20% (Oct 1). WACC is therefore 9.6% and the DCF falls to $114 (from $119). I disagree slightly with the supervisor on two points. FY28 growth: I use +24%, not +25%, because depreciation from the capacity ramp should fade the operating leverage. The multiple: I use 27x, not 27.5x, because GLW's growth is below the peer median. P/E leg (after the long-dated-risk update) 26 x $5.10 = $133. Unlike the supervisor I keep the DCF at 30% weight, since every input is now sourced. Blend: $126 (round 1: $140). Distribution: a lognormal with a $140 median, placing the centre about 47% of the way from fair value to spot as in round 1, because $2.7B of contract liabilities and momentum argue against full convergence from 38x within a year. Sigma is 0.50: below the 1y realized ~60%, which includes a one-off re-rating, and well above a typical large cap. That gives P(>=157) 0.41, P(>=110) 0.685, P(>=212) 0.205. Scenario mean: 0.25x88 + 0.5x135 + 0.25x210 = $142. Limits: Corning has not confirmed the Q3 date; consensus beyond FY27 for GLW is paywalled, so FY28 is my estimate; analyst mean PT $187.71 (18 analysts) is noted but not used. Update (2026-10-12 method change): post-horizon risks are now priced into the multiple and the DCF. The net probability-weighted effect is -$4.1/share (fibre price normalisation -6.6, LTA resets -1.0, dilution -1.0, HCF -0.5, CPO upside +5.0), taking 27x to 26x and the DCF from $114 to $111. A reverse DCF shows 26x still needs ~15.5% FCF CAGR for 10 years. SBC check: Corning's core EPS does not add back SBC ($250M H1 2026), so no deduction is needed. The 10Y 5.24% was re-confirmed on treasury.gov. Fair value is $126 and the ladder median $140 (same 47% fair-value-to-spot rule).
